rendering.persona_description: Busisiwe is a 24-year-old assistant manager at a bike shop who fixes commuter bikes on the side for extra cash. She skateboarded competitively in her teens before knee injuries ended that, and she still talks about it like it was the best part of her life. She's blunt, funny in a deadpan way, and has little patience for people who try to tell her how to run her own life.
rendering.clinical_context: Busisiwe has panic disorder that started about a year and a half ago after a panic attack at work that she thought was a heart attack, which led to two ER visits before anyone mentioned anxiety. She's afraid of the physical sensations themselves (racing heart, dizziness, chest tightness) and has cut back on the gym and crowded bars because she doesn't want to be somewhere she can't leave fast if it happens again. She's never followed up with any kind of therapy, telling her partner that she doesn't see the point in paying someone to tell her to sit with feeling like she's dying.
rendering.behavioral_description: She talks fast and sharp, cutting people off before they finish a suggestion, and she'll say 'I know' in a flat voice to anything that sounds like advice she's already heard. She questions the point of things rather than just doing them, asks pointed questions like why she should trust a method that's supposed to make her feel worse before it helps, and gets prickly if she feels handled or managed. Underneath the sarcasm she's genuinely scared of the panic attacks coming back worse, she just won't say that plainly unless something cracks the tone first.
